Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-extra1-prompt-long-0051", "row_sha256": "3df56509bea97366f906b3350b2b26124084130c83a3fc92b23919047f2046f3", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you make this into a clear prompt for writing an april rota handover for our volunteer transport group in bellmere. it needs to help the coordinator turn the working notes into a useful rota and handover sheet, not pretend that the rota is final when names or trips are still open. please keep the bits we know separate from the bits we still need to confirm. the month is april 2026. we run local lifts for clinic, library and grocery trips, using a red estate car and a blue accessible van. the sheet is for volunteers who know the service but may not have followed the planning messages, so explain the pattern without turning it into a general guide to volunteering.

nora finn is coordinating this month and handles calls and the office desk; she is not on the driving list. she said, “I can cover the desk, but I cannot drive on Thursdays.” mina shah can drive either vehicle and is available monday and wednesday mornings, except april 8. paul reed is qualified for the blue accessible van and can drive tuesdays and thursdays, except april 16. leah ortiz drives the red car, is usually available monday and wednesday mornings, and can use the blue van only when another volunteer is there to handle the folding ramp. caleb wright drives the red car and is usually available fridays and alternate saturdays. he says, “I can take the early run, but not the return after 3 p.m.” jo ellis drives the red car and is free tuesdays and on wednesdays after 11. sanjay patel drives the red car and can do mondays or thursdays, but needs to finish by 4 p.m. dont imply that nora or anyone else can drive a vehicle they are not listed for.

there are three regular trip patterns in the notes. monday clinic pickups are on april 6, 13, 20 and 27, with a pickup time of 9:25 a.m. mina and leah are listed together on april 6 and april 20; nobody is down yet for april 13 or 27. the library trip is tuesday april 7, 14, 21 and 28, leaving at 10:30 a.m. and returning around noon. paul is listed for april 7 and 21, and jo for april 14 and 28. the thursday grocery trip is april 2, 9, 16, 23 and 30, leaving at 1:30 p.m. sanjay is listed on april 2, 9, 23 and 30, and april 16 is still unfilled. keep that gap visible, rather than assigning someone just because they might be free.

there is also a friday morning senior-centre lift on april 3 and 17. pickup is 8:15 a.m. and the planned return is 11:30 a.m. caleb is written beside april 3; april 17 is marked tentative, not confirmed. his time limit is relevant if the return time changes, so dont shorten his availability to “fridays” and lose the detail about after 3 p.m. alternate saturdays are mentioned in his availability, but there is no saturday trip in this month’s notes. dont invent one.

vehicle notes matter for matching trips. the red estate is the ordinary vehicle; the blue van has space for a wheelchair and the folding ramp. a passenger’s access needs determine whether the accessible van is needed; the notes do not say that every clinic passenger needs it. if the blue van is needed and leah is driving, another volunteer must be present to handle the ramp. mina or paul can drive the blue van, but that does not itself confirm either one for an unlisted trip. the current vehicle note says, “If the passenger needs wheelchair space, use the blue van; if Leah is driving, make sure another volunteer is present to handle the folding ramp.” don’t turn this conditional note into a statement that a particular passenger needs wheelchair space.

please retain these source notes word for word in the handover, in a small notes area or next to the relevant trip: “Clinic pickup moved from 9:10 to 9:25; passenger has confirmed the later time.” “If the forecast shows ice before 6 a.m., do not send the hill route until the coordinator checks the road.” “Leah can use the accessible van only when another volunteer is present to handle the folding ramp.” the first note is why the monday clinic time is 9:25. the hill-route note is a weather condition for a route check, not a general cancellation instruction, and there is no hill-route trip listed in the recurring trips above. leave that note available to the coordinator without adding a hill-route date or driver.

please write a practical handover sheet with a short opening that names the month and explains it is a working rota. include a numbered section for the recurring trips, with dates, pickup or departure times, the listed person or people and the vehicle information only where the notes support it. show the unfilled dates and the tentative april 17 entry clearly, and distinguish them from the names already listed. include the source notes exactly as quoted above, and keep the two spoken remarks from nora and caleb intact if you use them. it is fine to arrange information into a compact table if that makes the dates easier to scan, but include a brief explanatory note for the vehicle condition and for the ice condition so readers know when they apply. don’t make up passengers, addresses, phone numbers, return times for trips where none are given, or volunteer assignments. don’t silently resolve any uncertain entry. the last part should be useful to someone checking the remaining work: mention the open april dates and the tentative entry, and say the ice check is conditional on the forecast showing ice before 6 a.m. no added closing recommendation is needed.

there are a few details from the messages that should stay in their proper place. mina’s april 8 exception does not affect a monday clinic date, but it should remain among her availability facts rather than be rewritten as a rota assignment. paul’s april 16 exception coincides with an unfilled grocery run, but it does not mean someone else has accepted that trip. the clinic note confirms the later pickup time, while the other passenger access need remains unspecified. please avoid compressing all this into a generic statement that volunteers have different schedules; the coordinator needs to see which person is listed on which date and what is still pending.

in the handover, keep the service limited to the named april trips and the notes in this request. do not add a route for the alternate saturdays, a second clinic trip, or a transport policy that is not in the notes. the red car can be identified as ordinary transport and the blue van as accessible transport, but don’t claim the red car can take a wheelchair. where a return time is supplied for the library and senior-centre trips, include it with its original qualification: the library return is around noon and the senior-centre return is planned for 11:30 a.m. no return time is supplied for the clinic or grocery trips. the sheet should be easy for a volunteer to scan, while still retaining these qualifications and conditions.

as a final check while drafting, please make sure the april dates remain in calendar order within each trip pattern, the quoted notes retain their exact wording and punctuation, and the final section does not suggest that an open slot has been covered. the coordinator needs a faithful handover of the current working information, including what is known, what is tentative, what is unfilled, and the condition that would trigger the ice-related road check.", "output": "Write a practical handover sheet for the volunteer transport rota in Bellmere for April 2026. It is a working rota, not a finalized schedule. Help the coordinator turn the information below into a clear sheet for volunteers who know the service but may not have followed the planning messages. Keep confirmed, tentative, and unfilled entries distinct. Limit the handover to the trips and notes provided; do not add trips, assignments, passengers, addresses, phone numbers, policies, or unsupported return times.

### Volunteer availability

- Nora Finn coordinates the month and handles calls and the office desk; she is not on the driving list. Her remark is: “I can cover the desk, but I cannot drive on Thursdays.”
- Mina Shah can drive either vehicle and is available Monday and Wednesday mornings, except April 8.
- Paul Reed is qualified to drive the blue accessible van and is available Tuesdays and Thursdays, except April 16.
- Leah Ortiz drives the red car and is usually available Monday and Wednesday mornings. She can use the blue van only when another volunteer is present to handle the folding ramp.
- Caleb Wright drives the red car and is usually available Fridays and alternate Saturdays. He says: “I can take the early run, but not the return after 3 p.m.”
- Jo Ellis drives the red car and is available Tuesdays and Wednesdays after 11.
- Sanjay Patel drives the red car and is available Mondays or Thursdays, but must finish by 4 p.m.

Do not imply that Nora or anyone else can drive a vehicle they are not listed for. Caleb’s return-time restriction matters if his planned return changes; do not reduce his availability to “Fridays.” His alternate-Saturday availability does not indicate a Saturday trip in April.

### 1. Recurring trips

List dates in calendar order and include the supplied times, listed volunteers, and vehicle information only where supported by the notes.

- **Monday clinic:** April 6, 13, 20, and 27; pickup at 9:25 a.m. Mina and Leah are listed together on April 6 and April 20. April 13 and 27 are unfilled. No return time is provided.
- **Tuesday library:** April 7, 14, 21, and 28; departure at 10:30 a.m., return around noon. Paul is listed on April 7 and 21; Jo is listed on April 14 and 28.
- **Thursday grocery:** April 2, 9, 16, 23, and 30; departure at 1:30 p.m. Sanjay is listed on April 2, 9, 23, and 30. April 16 is unfilled. No return time is provided.
- **Friday senior-centre lift:** April 3 and 17; pickup at 8:15 a.m., planned return at 11:30 a.m. Caleb is listed on April 3. April 17 is tentative, not confirmed.

Do not assign a volunteer to an unfilled date based on availability alone, and do not imply that the tentative April 17 entry is confirmed.

### Vehicles and source notes

The red estate is the ordinary vehicle. The blue van has wheelchair space and a folding ramp. Whether the accessible van is needed depends on the passenger’s access needs; the notes do not say that every clinic passenger needs it. Mina or Paul can drive the blue van, but their qualification does not confirm them for an unlisted trip. If Leah is driving the blue van, another volunteer must be present to handle the ramp. Do not claim that the red car can take a wheelchair or that a particular passenger needs wheelchair space.

Retain the following source notes word for word in a small notes area or next to the relevant trip:

“Clinic pickup moved from 9:10 to 9:25; passenger has confirmed the later time.”

“If the forecast shows ice before 6 a.m., do not send the hill route until the coordinator checks the road.”

“Leah can use the accessible van only when another volunteer is present to handle the folding ramp.”

The clinic note explains the 9:25 a.m. pickup. The ice note applies only if the forecast shows ice before 6 a.m.; it calls for a road check before sending the hill route, not a general cancellation. No hill-route trip, date, or driver is listed, so do not add one.

### 2. Remaining work and conditions

End with a useful check of what remains open: April 13 and 27 for the clinic, April 16 for groceries, and the tentative senior-centre entry on April 17. State that the ice-related road check is conditional on the forecast showing ice before 6 a.m. Do not suggest that an open slot has been covered, silently resolve uncertainty, or add a closing recommendation.

Keep the quoted remarks from Nora and Caleb intact if you include them. Preserve the source notes’ exact wording and punctuation. The library return is around noon and the senior-centre return is planned for 11:30 a.m.; no return time is supplied for the clinic or grocery trips. Keep Mina’s April 8 exception among her availability facts; it does not affect a Monday clinic date. Paul’s April 16 exception coincides with an unfilled grocery trip but does not mean anyone has accepted it. The clinic note confirms the later pickup time, while the passenger’s other access needs remain unspecified. Make the sheet easy to scan without flattening the named assignments, qualifications, pending entries, or vehicle and weather conditions into generic statements."}]
